title: B200 flex_attention_fwd 18% perf regression after #7565
body:
### Describe the issue

We are observing ~18% `flex_attention_fwd` TFLOPs regression happening on B200 after #7565 (b3b9931cb7ed07a6d7a3833c8dcb7b7b519e882f). Here are some stable perf results from TritonBench running `flex_attention_fwd` (N.B. the `compiled-tflops` field):

On ea4bdaf9d662e36a52ea422a37daa4e2e1abad30 (right before b3b9931cb7ed07a6d7a3833c8dcb7b7b519e882f):

```
             (B, Hq, M, Hkv, N, D) | Mask Type        eager-latency    eager-tflops    compiled-latency    compiled-tflops    compiled-speedup
----------------------------------------------  -------------------  --------------  ------------------  -----------------  ------------------
(8, 16, 2048, 16, 2048, 128) |            noop   12.421216 (±1.45%)         22.1297   0.673152 (±0.71%)            409.94              18.4523
(8, 16, 4096, 16, 4096, 128) |            noop   52.464802 (±0.00%)         20.9571   2.470944 (±0.25%)            446.715             21.2327
(8, 16, 8192, 16, 8192, 128) |            noop  266.076416 (±0.00%)         16.5293   9.525376 (±0.03%)            463.523             27.9334
                                       average                              19.872                                 440.059             22.5395
```

On b3b9931cb7ed07a6d7a3833c8dcb7b7b519e882f:

```
             (B, Hq, M, Hkv, N, D) | Mask Type        eager-latency    eager-tflops    compiled-latency    compiled-tflops    compiled-speedup
----------------------------------------------  -------------------  --------------  ------------------  -----------------  ------------------
(8, 16, 2048, 16, 2048, 128) |            noop   12.197824 (±4.43%)         22.535    0.807840 (±0.76%)            341.592             15.0993
(8, 16, 4096, 16, 4096, 128) |            noop   50.302177 (±0.00%)         21.8581   3.012736 (±0.10%)            366.38              16.6965
(8, 16, 8192, 16, 8192, 128) |            noop  240.981247 (±0.00%)         18.2506  11.689984 (±0.04%)            377.693             20.6143
                                       average                              20.8812                                361.888             17.4701
```

Here's a standalone script with the generated `flex_attention_fwd` kernel code that may help investigation: https://gist.github.com/reporter/76321caea3fcd969639a69f8aca6bf21 (courtesy of @participant3).

Can we please get some help in investigating and fixing the issue? CC @participant5 @participant2 @participant1. Thanks!

CC @participant1 @participant3 @participant6.

### Environment details

Triton: ea4bdaf9d662e36a52ea422a37daa4e2e1abad30 vs b3b9931cb7ed07a6d7a3833c8dcb7b7b519e882f
GPU: NVIDIA B200

> Can we please get some help in investigating and fixing the issue? CC [@participant5](https://github.com/participant5) [@participant2](https://github.com/participant2) [@participant1](https://github.com/participant1). Thanks!

I don't think we'll have bandwidth to investigate this.
I'm surprised you have a convert layout your attention main loop, do you know why? In the past we did notice high variance based on small changes on attention kernels, often due to different choices in scheduling, I wonder if that's what is going on.
I think someone will have to dig a bit more into that to root cause the problem as we haven't noticed performance regressions from this change.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: We compared the ttgir, ptx and ncu traces of the kernel runs on the commit right before the bisected PR and the commit with the PR. Here're our findings: - ttgir are unchanged, as expected - ptx differ primarily by `convert_layout` lowered to `ld.shared`/`st.shared` (the good one) vs `ldmatrix`/`stmatrix` (the bad one), and the number of load or store instructions in bad versions are also larger - one `convert_layout` of `128x64xbf16` in the loop looks outstanding - there's a huge increase in SMEM traffic in the bad version

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
also looking at the IR, it seems like we be doing a poor job picking the layout for the tmem_load which is causing the convert_layout to exist:
```
    %qk_95 = ttng.tmem_load %qk : !ttg.memdesc<128x64xf32, #tmem1, #ttng.tensor_memory, mutable> -> tensor<128x64xf32, #linear> loc(#loc231)
```

although I haven't looked in details at why this happens

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: You're right! Disabling `optimize_tmem_layouts` pass gives us 435 tflops. Perhaps we could look at this (simpler) pass to fix it. After all, there better not be any convert_layout in the loop at all.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: yeah sounds like a good workaround (although you could probably disable only 1 pattern in there)
